import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the datasets
pollen_df = pd.read_csv('/data/pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv')
time_series_df = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')
capital_df = pd.read_csv('/data/capital.csv')

# Extract the relevant column for daggers
dagger_data = time_series_df['Dagger']

# Calculate the rolling mean of the dagger data
rolling_mean = dagger_data.rolling(window=50).mean()

# Plot the original data and the rolling mean
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
plt.plot(time_series_df['CE'], dagger_data, label='Dagger Z values')
plt.plot(time_series_df['CE'], rolling_mean, label='Rolling mean of Dagger Z values')
plt.xlabel('CE')
plt.ylabel('Z values')
plt.title('Dagger Z values over time')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Load the datasets
pollen_df = pd.read_csv('/data/pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv')
time_series_df = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')
capital_df = pd.read_csv('/data/capital.csv')

# Extract the relevant column for daggers
dagger_data = time_series_df['Dagger']

# Calculate the rolling mean of the dagger data
rolling_mean = dagger_data.rolling(window=50).mean()

# Identify the point in time when the rolling mean starts to increase significantly
# For this, I will compare the rolling mean before and after a certain point in time
# Let's assume that the increase starts around CE 0 (the beginning of the Common Era)
# I will split the data into two parts: before and after CE 0
before_ce_0 = rolling_mean[time_series_df['CE'] < 0]
after_ce_0 = rolling_mean[time_series_df['CE'] >= 0]

# Perform a t-test to compare the means of the two groups
t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(before_ce_0, after_ce_0)

t_stat, p_value

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the datasets
pollen_df = pd.read_csv('/data/pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv')
time_series_df = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')
capital_df = pd.read_csv('/data/capital.csv')

# Extract the relevant column for daggers
dagger_data = time_series_df['Dagger']

# Calculate the rolling mean of the dagger data
rolling_mean = dagger_data.rolling(window=50).mean()

# Drop the first few rows with missing values in the rolling mean
rolling_mean_clean = rolling_mean.dropna()

# Extract the corresponding CE values
ce_values_clean = time_series_df['CE'][rolling_mean_clean.index]

# Plot the cleaned rolling mean
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
plt.plot(ce_values_clean, rolling_mean_clean, label='Rolling mean of Dagger Z values')
plt.xlabel('CE')
plt.ylabel('Z values')
plt.title('Cleaned Rolling Mean of Dagger Z values over time')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
